newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech major shares slide, dragging PX50 lower.
newsitem.headline: Czech major shares slide, dragging PX50 lower.

text.p: Czech major issues posted across-the-board losses on Tuesday with analysts and dealers seeing little hope of a substantial upturn until foreign investor apathy towards eastern European bourses subsides.
The PX50 fell 5.0 points, 0.86 percent, to 579.5 while the major issue dominated RPIX index -- most of whose shares are also on the PX50 -- lost 13.5 points, 1.1 percent, to 1,218.1.
"Generally it is caused by lack of demand because there are no new orders from abroad and domestic speculators see no reason to buy," said Pavel Sobisek of Zivnostenska Banka.
"People are just sitting and watching," added Radim Bajgar of ING Barings.
Most of the downward pressure was applied by the four most heavily weighted shares -- SPT Telecom, CEZ Komercni Banka and Ceska Sporitelna -- which taken together fell by an average of 1.6 percent.

Bajgar said the current stagnation on the Prague bourse was caused by a combination of the generally bearish sentiment among foreign dealers about the region's equity markets and pessimistic predictions about the Czech economy in 1997.
Added to this, he said, financial results for 1996, from the leading companies which have released them, have failed to impress the market.
"What's most important is the position of EPS (earnings per share). This year we saw a slight weakening compared with brokerages (earlier) predictions," he said referring to the major issues.
One bright spot on the PX50, was provided by tobacco company Tabak which built on Monday's 199 crown again with a further rise of 100 crowns to 8,400.
"Speculation about their profitability, and very, very good dividends they could pay out again (are responsible for the rise)," said Bajgar.
Overall, turnover was little changed at 1.1 billion crowns with volume at 1,155,161 shares.
Adavancers beat decliners by 230 to 212 and 153 issues were unchanged.
